mission_02: Differentiable reasoning extends classical logic to continuous truth values in [0,1], enabling gradient-based optimization of logical constraints. Using fuzzy logic operations — product t-norm for AND, probabilistic sum for OR, standard negation for NOT, and Reichenbach implication — logical formulas become differentiable functions of their input truth values. This allows neural networks to be trained with logical constraints as soft penalties. In this mission, you implement fuzzy logic operators, a recursive formula evaluator that parses nested logical expressions, and gradient computation via numerical differentiation. The gradients tell us how to adjust truth values to make a formula more or less true, enabling end-to-end learning with logical supervision.
